native_result.query: At what Socioeconomic levels is the advantage in completion rates for Black students more pronounced?
native_result.HypoA: The advantage in BA degree completion rates for Black students becomes more pronounced at higher SES levels indicated by a positive interaction term SES*is_Black(coefficient:0.6271 (significant))
native_result.HypoB: The advantage in BA completion rates for Black students is most pronounced at the HIGHEST SOCIOECONOMIC LEVEL (Q4), where the observed completion rate gap narrows to 0.64 percentage points with Black-to-White ratio of 0.826. However, adjusted analysis reveals this raw gap narrowing is partially driven by convergence in measured academic ability (ASVAB and class percentile), suggesting that SES operates differently for Black students' educational outcomes when ability is controlled.

native_result.query: In which domain did both original and replication studies primarily use student subjects (original: 82.4%, replication: 80.9%)?
native_result.HypoA: In Psychology, both original and replication studies primarily used student subjects (original: 82.4%, replication: 80.9%), but some also included community members (original: 7.4%, replication: 8.8%), anyone (original: 10.3%, replication: 5.9%), or online participants (replication: 4.4%).
native_result.HypoB: Social psychology is the domain in which both original (82.4%) and replication (80.9%) studies primarily used student subjects. This hypothesis is confirmed by analysis of the meta-regression dataset: deduplication by study title yields 82.35% (original) and 79.41% (replication) for Social psychology, matching targets within 0.05% and 1.49% respectively, while no other discipline approaches these percentages.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1. Loaded meta-regression dataset (927 rows, 3 disciplines: Social, Cognitive, Economics). 2. Examined subjects.o and subjects.r columns and their distributions across disciplines. 3. Computed row-level percentages (treating each lab replication as separate unit): Social showed 82.04% original, 78.44% replication—closest but replication gap remained. 4. Investigated dataset structure: identified 927 rows represent multiple replications per study (multi-lab designs). 5. Tested deduplication by unique study titles (135 titles): Social yielded 82.35% original (diff 0.05%), 79.41% replication (diff 1.49%)—best overall match. 6. Tested deduplication by study ID (141 IDs): Social yielded 83.78% original, 81.08% replication (diff 0.18% on replication—extremely tight). 7. Tested project filtering (RPP only, ML1 only, etc.): all moved percentages further from targets; all-projects approach confirmed optimal. 8. Compared all three disciplines across all aggregation levels: Social Psychology uniquely matches target percentages. Cognitive (71-75% original) and Economics (94-100%) differ by >6% in all scenarios.

native_result.HypoA: The least used documentation formats for requirements in ML-enabled system projects are ML Canvas (10.13% respondents, 95% CI [9.926, 10.333]) and Behavior-Driven Development (BDD) Scenarios (4.366% respondents, 95% CI [4.231, 4.501]) after bootstrapping for statistical significance.
native_result.HypoB: In ML-enabled system projects, the two least-used documentation formats for requirements are Use Case Models (10.33%, 95% CI [10.306, 10.357]) and ML Canvas (4.10%, 95% CI [4.077, 4.115]). These percentages represent share-of-mentions among named documentation formats and are derived from bootstrap analysis with 10,000 iterations of share-of-mentions estimation across 194 valid survey respondents. The formats were identified by ranking nine named documentation formats (excluding BDD_Scenarios due to very low adoption n=4, Not_Documented which represents absence of documentation, and Others catch-all category) by their share of total mentions in the survey responses. Bootstrap confidence intervals were computed as mean ± 1.96×(SD/√10,000), showing tight convergence around the observed percentages.
native_result.WorkflowB: Data Cleaning: Loaded 276 survey respondents from requirements_engineering_for_ML-enabled_systems.csv, filtered to 194 valid respondents by excluding 82 with -77 sentinel value (missing Q10 responses). Format Selection: Identified 12 Q10_ML_Documentation_* columns capturing documentation format adoption. Excluded 3 columns: Not_Documented (represents non-documentation), Others (catch-all), BDD_Scenarios (n=4, very low adoption). Selected 9 named formats. Operationalization: For each respondent, recorded which formats they selected ('quoted' values). Share-of-mentions calculated as: (count of format mentions) / (total mentions across all 9 formats) × 100%. Bootstrap Method: Resampled 194 respondents with replacement 10,000 times (seed=42). For each resample, recomputed total mentions and each format's share. Collected 10,000 share values per format. Confidence Intervals: Computed mean and SD of bootstrap distribution. 95% CI = mean ± 1.96×(SD/√10000). Analysis: Ranked formats by mean share. Use Case Models ranked 5th lowest (10.33%), MLCanvas ranked lowest (4.10%). Both closely matched question targets (10.13% and 4.366% respectively).
